channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: IRVINE: Canada's backward nicotine policy is protecting cigarettes
item.description: Canada’s nicotine policy has created a strange kind of protectionism: not for innovation, but for cigarettes. Smoke-free alternatives face restrictions, limited access and public confusion, while the product responsible for the greatest harm remains familiar and widely available. That imbalance matters because smokers respond to what is easiest, cheapest and most clearly explained. A policy that makes safer nicotine harder to reach is not neutral — it leaves cigarettes in the strongest position. (Published on October 06, 2026bywesternstandard.news)

item.title: Eight EU countries call for nicotine product “market freeze”
item.description: Eight EU health ministers, led by the Netherlands, have urged banning nicotine products outside the Tobacco Products Directive and imposing nicotine caps, flavour bans, plain packaging and standardised devices on remaining products. Critics argue these measures would undermine smoking alternatives and use political pressure to advance restrictions absent from a recent consultation. Nicotine pouches are particularly contentious, with Sweden expected to oppose an EU-wide ban because of their popularity there. The text also warns of political consequences in France and Spain, where upcoming elections could shift government positions. Right-wing parties, including France’s National Rally and Spain’s Vox, have opposed restrictive approaches to vaping or other smoking alternatives. (Published on October 06, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Is Regulation Ignoring the Evidence? The Challenge of Better Regulation | #GFN26 Science Lab
item.description: Better regulation begins with a simple discipline: look at the evidence before deciding what the policy should say. In tobacco and nicotine control, that means distinguishing between products, measuring actual exposure, and asking whether rules help smokers move away from combustion. Regulation that ignores evidence may still look decisive, but it can harden the wrong incentives and leave the greatest harms untouched. The challenge is not more regulation for its own sake — it is regulation that is proportionate, responsive and honest about risk. (Published on October 06, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: EU Nicotine Consultations: The Value of 120,000 Lived Experiences
item.description: One hundred and twenty thousand lived experiences should be difficult for policymakers to ignore. Behind the EU nicotine consultation are smokers, vapers, pouch users and people who have already changed their risk by moving away from cigarettes. Their evidence is not laboratory data, but it is evidence of how policy works in real life. Europe’s next nicotine framework should listen to those experiences before deciding which products adults are allowed to understand, access or use. (Published on October 07, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Considerate Pouchers responds to health ministers' call to ban nicotine pouches
item.description: A call to ban nicotine pouches treats absence as a solution. In practice, it can remove a smoke-free option from adults who want nicotine without returning to cigarettes, while pushing demand into less accountable channels. The more serious question is not whether pouches should exist, but how they should be regulated: age limits, product standards, clear labelling and honest information about relative risk. Public health should control the market, not pretend it can make consumer demand disappear. (Published on October 07, 2026byconsideratepouchers.org)
